title: Ayotzinapa Back in Spotlight – Soberanía 119
author: Mexico Solidarity
content:
In episode 119 of Soberanía, hosts José Luis Granados Ceja and Kurt Hackbarth
cover the long-awaited development in the case of the forcibly disappeared 43
Ayotzinapa students with the arrest of former Guerrero Governor Ángel Aguirre
Rivero. While the hosts welcome this development, they note that the
investigation remains stalled by stonewalling, and that the National Human
Rights Commission's recent report effectively exonerated the armed forces,
drawing fierce protests from victims' families and activists.

Next, they dissect the State Department's extraordinary five-minute video
glorifying the Monroe Doctrine, openly celebrating U.S. "dominance" over the
hemisphere and even taking credit for Mexico's defeat of the Habsburg monarchy
(which was actually achieved by Benito Juárez and the Mexican people). The
hosts argue this "saying the quiet part out loud" moment reveals what U.S.
policy has always been: not cooperation, but imperial domination.

The conversation then turns to South America. They run down Colombian
President Abelardo de la Espirella's first days in office — a whirlwind of
embarrassing behavior, recognizing Israel's claim to the Golan Heights,
backing out of the Belt and Road Initiative, and refusing earthquake aid —
before noting positive developments: Mexico's foreign minister met with Lula
in Brazil, diplomatic relations with Peru have been restored, and Argentina
saw mass protests against Milei's plan to sell off national territory to
foreign interests.

Losers and Haters takes aim once again at PRI president Alejandro Moreno, who
traveled to Washington to request U.S. sanctions against Mexican electoral
officials — yet another embarrassing display of a "vendepatria" begging for
foreign intervention while corruption investigations close in on him at home.
